item.title: O canto dos pássaros como sinal de segurança
item.description: O seu cérebro tem um circuito antigo que monitoriza, de forma constante e subconsciente, se há pássaros a cantar. É descrito como um sistema de deteção de predadores que os mamíferos usam há cerca de 200 milhões de anos. Um silêncio súbito no canto dos pássaros sinalizava historicamente a proximidade de uma ameaça.

item.title: Vogelgesang als Sicherheitssignal
item.description:
Ihr Gehirn besitzt einen uralten Schaltkreis, der ständig und unterbewusst überprüft, ob Vögel singen. Beschrieben wird er als ein System zur Erkennung von Raubtieren, das Säugetiere seit rund 200 Millionen Jahren nutzen. Ein plötzliches Verstummen des Vogelgesangs signalisierte historisch eine drohende Gefahr.

Ein paar Befunde, auf die ich gestoßen bin:

item.title: Пение птиц как сигнал безопасности
item.description:
Ваш мозг имеет древний механизм, который постоянно и бессознательно отслеживает, поют ли птицы. Его описывают как систему обнаружения хищников, которой млекопитающие пользуются уже примерно 200 миллионов лет. Внезапное прекращение пения птиц исторически сигнализировало о наличии угрозы.

Несколько находок, на которые я наткнулся:

  • Пение птиц снижает тревожность и депрессию. Исследование 2022 года Института Макса Планка показало, что всего шесть минут пения птиц уменьшают тревожность, тогда как такое же время шума транспорта усиливает симптомы депрессии.
  • Повышает «расслабленную бдительность». Данные ЭЭГ показывают, что пение птиц при уровне громкости 45–50 децибел (как тихий разговор) увеличивает активность альфа-волн мозга на 14,1%, что связано с состоянием спокойной сосредоточенности.
  • Положительное влияние на настроение может длиться часами. Исследование Королевского колледжа Лондона с участием более 1200 человек показало, что улучшение настроения от пения птиц сохраняется в течение нескольких часов после того, как звук прекращается.

item.title: Andor, Season 2
item.description:
The best thing Star Wars has done in decades. Tony Gilroy writing adult political drama with grown-up pacing and stakes. The prison arc in S1 was already a small miracle; S2 keeps the bar there for twelve episodes.

Watch even if you don’t care about Star Wars. Especially if you don’t.

item.title: Binary Search — and how I kept getting it wrong
item.description:
Binary search is the algorithm I’ve “known” the longest and written incorrectly the most times. The issue is never the idea. It’s the off-by-one.

The canonical bug

# Wrong on the edges
def bs(nums, target):
 lo, hi = 0, len(nums)
 while lo < hi:
 mid = (lo + hi) // 2
 if nums[mid] == target:
 return mid
 elif nums[mid] < target:
 lo = mid # ← infinite loop
 else:
 hi = mid
 return -1

lo = mid without + 1 stalls when lo + 1 == hi.

item.title: Outer Wilds
item.description:
Finally played Outer Wilds. It lives up to the reputation — probably the purest expression of curiosity-as-gameplay I’ve ever seen. No combat, no upgrades, no gear checks. Just you, a ship, and a solar system full of things that deserve to be understood.

Spoilers would genuinely hurt the experience, so I’ll just say: every “aha” moment lands, and the structure of the final act is audacious.

item.title: Severance, Season 2
item.description:
The aesthetic is doing an incredible amount of work. Every frame is composed like a Wes Anderson cover of a Kafka short story. The plot moves slower than it thinks it does, but the atmosphere carries it.

The “innies vs outies” ethics keep finding new dimensions. I suspect the show is structurally incapable of landing a finale that matches the premise, but the ride is the point.

item.title: Valid Parentheses
item.description:
Problem

Given a string of brackets ()[]{}, determine whether it is valid — every opening bracket has a matching closing bracket, and they are properly nested.

Solution

Classic stack problem. Push opening brackets, pop and compare on closing.

def isValid(s: str) -> bool:
 pairs = {")": "(", "]": "[", "}": "{"}
 stack = []
 for ch in s:
 if ch in "([{":
 stack.append(ch)
 elif not stack or stack.pop() != pairs[ch]:
 return False
 return not stack

Complexity

  • Time: O(n)
  • Space: O(n) — worst case the stack is as long as the input.

item.title: Tunic
item.description:
A small fox with a sword, a cryptic in-game manual written in an invented script, and a world that reveals a second, far deeper layer once you start translating the runes. The first 10 hours feel like Zelda homage; the next 20 feel like the most clever ARG I’ve played in years.

Not for everyone — if “read the manual” isn’t your idea of gameplay, skip. For me, peak satisfaction.

item.title: X-Files, 2x18 - Fearful Symmetry
item.description:
Epic continuation of Denis Villeneuve’s adaptation. The scale, visuals, and sound design are absolutely stunning. Timothée Chalamet and Zendaya deliver powerful performances.

The way Villeneuve translates Herbert’s complex narrative into pure cinema is masterful. Every frame is meticulously crafted. Hans Zimmer’s score elevates the entire experience.

Best watched in IMAX.

item.title: Two Sum
item.description:
Problem

Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target.

Solution

The brute force approach would be O(n²), but we can optimize it using a hash table to achieve O(n) time complexity.

def twoSum(nums, target):
 seen = {}
 for i, num in enumerate(nums):
 complement = target - num
 if complement in seen:
 return [seen[complement], i]
 seen[num] = i
 return []

Complexity

  • Time: O(n) - single pass through the array
  • Space: O(n) - hash table storage

Key Insights

Using a hash table allows us to look up complements in constant time, reducing the overall complexity from O(n²) to O(n).

item.title: Heretic
item.description:
I’ve always loved dark fantasy aesthetics, and Heretic remains one of the best representatives of the genre. Built on id Tech 1 (the Doom engine), it perfectly captures that gritty, supernatural atmosphere.

First played this back in the 90s on MS-DOS. Recently revisited it through the Steam release with enhanced graphics, improved music, and proper mouse support. Pure nostalgia.
